doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Launeddas in Sardinia with Paolo Fresu; Ed Sarath's date
summary: He recorded in Sardinia with the last master of the 3,000-year-old launeddas pipes, and mentions meeting Billy Hart and Cecil McBee as a team on Ed Sarath's record.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Here’s an interesting looking one – it was done in Milan – of yours called The Blessing of the Old, Long Sound.

Launeddas. I went to – what’s the city I went to? Sardinia, with Paolo Fresu, who had – was not known then. Had a band. Invited me. Toured with him. In fact, Caris was on that tour. Recorded there. The launeddas is the Sardinian instrument. It is a – do you know what it is?

It’s three pipes. One is the drone. One is a fourth and fifth with this finger. And one is – I guess four notes. So it’s a triple – what do you call it? – circular breathing. 3,000 years old. They have absolute proof it was 3,000 years old. I’m always interested in where I go, bah bah boom. Could I meet the guy? I meet the master, the last living master. Name is Baranka, old cat, chain-smoking cigarettes, little Italian, 75 years old, playing the shit out of this thing. So the record date, it was arranged to meet – Liebman
meets launeddas. We did India. We did Richie’s Elm. They arranged three different cats to play launeddas to play the chords. That’s a kind of interesting record, folky type thing, ethnic.
Then you – there’s a follow up. The same dates, it says, all for – the label is called Nueva. It’s an Italian label. Here’s an interesting Ed Sarath date, Voice of the Wind.

This is where I first got the idea of Billy and Cecil as a team. That’s Ed’s record. Ed came through University of Michigan. How did I meet Ed? I don’t know. Maybe through IASJ. I don’t remember how we first met.
